Race Against Time
On June 21, 1964, civil rights workers James Chaney, Michael Schwerner, and Andrew Goodman were murdered in Neshoba County, Mississippi by members of the Mississippi White Knights of the KKK.

...

No one was tried or convicted of murder at the time.
Jerry Mitchell, a pale-skinned red-headed reporter for the Jackson Clarion-Ledger first got interested in the Schwerner, Chaney, and Goodman case after watching the Mississippi Burning movie in 1988.  In Race Against Time , he tells his story of tracking down the remaining remnants of four unresolved cases from the 1960s. Mitchell’s input mattered. And he gives the reader a window into the violence that was used to defend the Jim Crow Era.
Mitchell finds Rita Schwerner Bender, the widow of the deceased Michael, significantly helpful.

1. Jerry Mitchell

Jerry Mitchell

GRANTEE
The stories of Jerry Mitchell, who leads the investigative reporting team for Mississippi Today, have helped put four Klansmen and a serial killer behind bars as well as helping free two people from death row.
Mitchell is a two-time Pulitzer Prize finalist and a winner of more than 30 other national awards, including a $500,000 MacArthur “genius” grant. He is the author of Race Against Time , which is about his pursuit of some of the nation's most notorious murders, including the 1963 assassination of civil rights activist Medgar Evers and the KKK’s 1964 killings of three civil rights workers.
The Mississippi Today investigative reporting team has exposed a two-decade reign of terror by officers called the "Goon Squad."
